source: ChemSep v8.3 pure component data (Copyright (c) Harry Kooijman and Ross Taylor; Artistic License 2.0), as embedded in DWSIM 10.2.5 (DWSIM.Thermodynamics.dll resource chemsep1.xml), compound "Hydrogen sulfide" (ChemSep index 1922, CAS 7783-06-4). Molecular weight, normal boiling point, Tc, Pc and acentric factor as given; standard liquid density: eq. 105 saturated liquid at 288.7056 K (60 F), as the bundled light ends; ideal-gas Cp eq. 16 (A=33121.9, B=-869.6079, C=9.605736, D=0.00110059, E=-3.859399e-7; data 50..1500 K) fitted by least squares as shifted_polynomial_5 over 187.68..900 K (30 points), largest deviation -0.007 % at 221.7 K, 0.004 % over 298.15..900 K; viscosity tables and freezing data in their entries. Imported by tools/compound-import.

fluid_domain.evidence: Fluid network only (not the column range): the ideal-gas Cp fit range, from max(ChemSep Cp data start, triple point) to 900 K; below it Cp is held and integrated, with a notice (a data-range end, never a validity floor). 100 Pa..2000000 Pa as the bundled light ends: PR78 from ChemSep critical constants, not qualified above that.

thermochemistry.source: Ideal-gas heat of formation at 298.15 K and formula H2S (molar mass 34.076 g/mol) of ChemSep v8.3 pure component data (Copyright (c) Harry Kooijman and Ross Taylor; Artistic License 2.0), as embedded in DWSIM 10.2.5 (DWSIM.Thermodynamics.dll resource chemsep1.xml), compound "Hydrogen sulfide" (ChemSep index 1922, CAS 7783-06-4). Heats of reaction follow by Hess's law. Data only.

flammability.source: NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards, Hydrogen sulfide (npgd0337, https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/npg/npgd0337.html, read 2026-11-05): LEL and UEL in air. CDC material, in the public domain. Constant with temperature (owner decision E23).

combustion.source: Hess's law on this record's thermochemistry (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1): the formula burnt to CO2, H2O (gas), SO2 and N2 on the ideal-gas heats of formation at 298.15 K of icheme:chemsep_carbon_dioxide (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1), icheme:water (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1) and icheme:chemsep_sulfur_dioxide (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1). Computed by tools/heating-values/heating-values.mjs. Read by a fired heater's burners.

henry_in_water.source: IAPWS G7-04, Guideline on the Henry's Constant and Vapor-Liquid Distribution Constant for Gases in H2O and D2O at High Temperatures (2004), after R. Fernandez-Prini, J. L. Alvarez, A. H. Harvey, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 32 (2003) 903, table of A, B, C for H2S in H2O: ln(kH/p*) = A/Tr + B tau^0.355/Tr + C Tr^-0.41 exp(tau), Tr = T/647.096 K, tau = 1 - Tr, p* the saturation pressure of water, kH on the mole-fraction basis. Coefficients as in Table 2 of the guideline (iapws.org, read 2026-11-11). Copyright 2004 IAPWS; publication in whole or in part is allowed provided attribution is given to IAPWS.
